subject.title: feat: version field in health response + POST /admin/update endpoint

question: Should OpenClaw expose host update execution through an authenticated HTTP operator surface, and if so should it reuse the default-off Admin HTTP RPC plugin instead of adding a bespoke `/admin/update` endpoint?
rationale: Current main already has `update.run` as an admin-scoped Gateway RPC and has a default-off authenticated Admin HTTP RPC plugin, but allowing package-manager update execution over HTTP changes a high-power operator boundary.

options.title: Reuse Admin HTTP RPC after approval
options.body: Add `update.run` to the default-off Admin HTTP RPC plugin with explicit private-ingress docs, schema/tests, and upgrade proof if maintainers approve HTTP update execution.

options.title: Keep update execution off HTTP
options.body: Leave `update.run` on WebSocket/Gateway RPC paths only and direct fleet tooling to those supported clients or a local trusted helper.

options.title: Design a bespoke endpoint
options.body: Create a separate authenticated update endpoint only if maintainers decide the RPC shape cannot safely support fleet tooling.

recommendation.title: Reuse Admin HTTP RPC after approval
recommendation.body: Add `update.run` to the default-off Admin HTTP RPC plugin with explicit private-ingress docs, schema/tests, and upgrade proof if maintainers approve HTTP update execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Admin HTTP RPC plugin and have the strongest adjacent ownership signal for the HTTP operator boundary.
